description.narrative: Stöd till civilsamhällesorganisation som arbetar i Mekongregionen för att stärka lokala samhällens mänskliga rättigheter, skydd för miljön och verka för klimaträttvisa.
Support to NGO supporting local communities in the Mekong region to protect their human rights, the Environment and request accountability for the climate crisis.

The objective of the intervention is to contribute to the implementation of EarthRights Mekong Regional Program, which is aligned to contribute to the realisation of EarthRight's global strategic plan 2020-2024.
The Regional goals and objectives of the Mekong Regional Program are:
Regional goal 1 - Climate Justice and Accountability
Regional goal 2 - Earth Rights Defenders
Regional Goal 3 - Corporate Accountability
The program is also intended, to the extent relevant for the Mekong Regional Program, to contribute to four of EarthRights six Global Operational Goals:
1. Gender Justice and Social Inclusion.
2. Development and implementation of Physical and Cyber Security Protection
3. Development of an organisational monitoring and evaluation system that will include annual planning, data collection and learning processes to inform program design and goal-setting.
4. Increased policy and research capacity through development of human and financial resources and partnerships

The Embassy assesses that ERI's Mekong regional programme has delivered strong results within the three regional goals despite operating in difficult contexts. The programme has adopted to the changes in the areas of operations, shifting modalities during COVID19 and after the Myanmar coup, while still achieving outcomes and impacts that contributed to the result areas. The external evaluation in 2023, and the Embassys obsrervation, raise ERIs longterm partnership model, communitydriven evidence, and legal expertise as core drivers of effectiveness.
Regional Goal 1 Community Power and Agency
Between 20202025, ERI strengthened communities capacity to document environmental harms and advocate for remedies. Communityled research became more systematic, safer and more credible, with several groups producing evidence on hydropower, mining and landuse impacts that was later used by local authorities, journalists and civil society coalitions. In multiple cases, this evidence contributed to adjustments in project design, mitigation measures or compensation processes. The programmes relevance increased as civic space shrank in Laos and Cambodia and closed in Myanmar. The results of increased skills and strengthened community networks should have good possibilities to remain after phasing out.
Regional Goal 2 Earth Rights Defenders
ERI significantly improved the safety, resilience and effectiveness of EHRD. The EHRD strengthened their digital and physical security practices, coordinated more effectively through crossborder protection networks. Through the EarthRights School and alumni programme, defenders gained advanced skills in research, communication, negotiation and project management, and many began leading their own advocacy initiatives with reduced reliance on ERI. ERIs legal accompaniment supported strategic complaints that contributed to project suspensions, corrective actions and improved compensation processes. In Myanmar, adapted remote support enabled defenders to continue documenting abuses under extreme repression.
Regional Goal 3 Corporate Accountability
ERI contributed to increased scrutiny and accountability of corporate and financial actors. ERIsupported complaints, such as the OECD case against MTI Energy, triggered formal reviews and heightened international attention to duediligence failures in Myanmars extractive sector.
International financial institutions used ERIs fieldverified evidence to strengthen safeguard requirements and delay or reconsider financing for highrisk projects. At the company level, ERIsupported community monitoring in Cambodia and Laos led to concrete operational changes, including improved wastemanagement systems, erosioncontrol measures and more transparent consultation processes. These results demonstrate that ERI contributed to increased accountability in a region where regulatory frameworks remain weak.
